pages.title: Shopping for clothes

situation.text: You are in a clothing store. You like a jacket, but you need a different size and color. You ask the price, try it on and decide.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can ask the price, ask for another size or color, try something on and say if it fits.
canDo: Ask the price: How much is…?
Ask for size or color: Do you have this in…?
Ask to try something on: Can I try it on?
Say how it fits: It’s too big / It fits!
success: I ask for another size or color.
I try it on and say how it fits.
I decide and thank the seller.
pages.think: When you buy clothes in Brazil, what do you ask first: the price, the size or the color? Is it the same in English?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação de compra: uma jaqueta, um tamanho errado e uma decisão.
solo: Pergunte: “O que você faz quando a roupa não serve?” em português, depois em inglês simples.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso.
group: Cada estudante diz uma peça de roupa em inglês (jacket, shirt, shoes…).
Mostre a cena e pergunte: Where are they? What are they buying?
extra: What is your favorite piece of clothing?
Do you like shopping?
support: Mostre figuras e aceite palavras soltas: jacket, blue, big.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Recycle routines and move to shopping.
intro.group: Each student asks one question and the next person answers.

pages.recall: Talking about routines: “What time do you…? / I usually…”. Ask: What time do you usually go shopping?

qs.pt: O que você está vestindo hoje?
Qual é a sua cor favorita?

teach.goal: Revisar rotina e abrir o vocabulário de roupas e cores.
extra: When do you usually buy clothes?
Do you shop online or in stores?
support: Aponte para as roupas da sala e peça só a palavra.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Shopping in the USA
pages.intro: Shopping in the USA has small surprises: sizes, tax at the register and return policies. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: The price tag usually does not include sales tax. It is added at the register, so you pay a little more.
US, UK and Brazilian sizes are different. A US size 8 is not the same as a Brazilian 38. Check the size chart!
You can try clothes on in a fitting room. Many stores accept returns with a receipt, but each store has its own rule.

qs.q: Why is the final price higher than the tag?
qs.pt: Por que o preço final é maior que a etiqueta?

levels.A2: In the USA, sales tax is added at the register.
levels.B1: The tag usually shows the price before sales tax, which is added when you pay.
levels.B2: Unlike in Brazil, where the displayed price normally includes taxes, US stores add sales tax at checkout, and the rate depends on the state.

qs.q: What do you do if you are not sure about the size?
qs.pt: O que fazer se você não tem certeza do tamanho?

levels.A2: You can try it on or ask for a different size.
levels.B1: Try it on in the fitting room and ask the seller for a bigger or smaller size.
levels.B2: Ask to try it on, and compare with the store’s size chart, because sizes vary by brand and country.

qs.q: Can you return something you bought?
qs.pt: Dá para devolver o que você comprou?

levels.A2: Many stores accept returns if you have the receipt.
levels.B1: Many stores accept returns within a certain number of days if you keep the receipt and the tags.
levels.B2: Return policies differ by store, so it is wise to ask “What’s your return policy?” before buying.

pages.compare: In Brazil the displayed price normally already includes taxes, and you can usually try on clothes without asking. How does it work where you shop?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural: preço sem imposto, tamanhos e provador.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare a etiqueta brasileira (com imposto) com a americana (sem imposto).
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “What size are you in Brazil?”.
answers: Q1: sales tax added at the register.
Q2: try it on; ask for another size.
Q3: often with receipt; rules differ by store.
extra: What size are you in Brazil?
Have you returned something to a store?
support: Use as respostas A1 como modelo.
stretch: B2: discuta vantagens de mostrar o preço com ou sem imposto.

pass1.pt: O que a cliente está fazendo?

teach.goal: Entender preço, cor e tamanhos antes de ver o texto.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: situação. 2ª escuta: preço, cor, tamanhos, pagamento.
Mostre o texto depois.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam.
Compare as respostas.
answers: Pass 2: forty dollars · blue · medium · small · card.
extra: Is the jacket on sale?
Why does Lily ask for small?

opts: The medium is a little big.

items.use: Ask the price of one thing.
items.alt: More than one: **How much are these?**

items.use: Ask for another size or color.
Ask to use the fitting room.
Say why it does not work.
The seller asks how you will pay.

items.en: Do you have this in black?

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again today: How much is…? · Do you have this in…? · Can I try it on?

teach.goal: Escolher 4 chunks e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de traduzir.
Peça um exemplo com uma peça de roupa do aluno.
group: Cada estudante escolhe uma expressão e dá um exemplo.
Duplas: pergunte o preço de 3 objetos da sala.
answers: Asking the price · Asking for options · Trying on · Describing fit · Deciding

What is the opposite of “too big”?
support: Use só How much is…? e Can I try it on? na primeira rodada.

patterns.name: Asking the price
patterns.formula: **How much is** + this / that / it? (**are** + these / those)
ex: How much is it with tax?

patterns.name: Asking for another size or color
patterns.formula: **Do you have this in** + size / color?
ex: Do you have this in blue?
Do you have this in small?
Do you have these in black?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: What is the price of this item?
Will you be paying by cash or by card?
register.note: In stores people use short, friendly phrases. Written English (labels, emails) is more formal.

teach.goal: Fixar “How much is…?” e “Do you have this in…?”; os demais são expansão.
solo: Mostre os padrões DENTRO do diálogo.
Troque as peças e peça a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça.
Pares: A é vendedor, B é cliente.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão.

Change the color and size.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Yes/no questions often go up at the end: “Can I try it on?” ↗. Questions with how/what go down: “How much is it?” ↘.

items.say: Do you have this in blue?
items.linked: Do you have this in BLUE? ↗

own.prompt: Write one yes/no question and one “how much” question about something in your bag.
own.criteria: Say them: the yes/no goes up, the “how much” goes down.

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: entonação ascendente (yes/no) e descendente (wh-).
solo: Desenhe a seta com a mão: sobe/desce.
Peça que o estudante diga as duas perguntas com a entonação certa.
group: Coro com gesto; duplas ouvindo a seta.
Cada estudante diz as próprias perguntas.
answers: Identify 1: Can I try it on? · Identify 2: How much is it?

errors.w: How much is it? (sobe no final)
Can I try it on. (desce, parece ordem)

support: Use gestos com a mão para sobe/desce.

pages.title: Group mission — the shopping trip
pages.goal: Each group must buy something in English: ask, try, decide and pay.

missions.mission: Buy a pair of shoes in black. Your size is not in stock. Ask for another color.
missions.constraint: Ask “How much are…?” and “Do you have these in…?”

missions.mission: Buy a gift shirt for a friend. Find the right size and the price you can pay.
missions.constraint: Use “Can I try it on?” once.
missions.start: Hi! Do you have this in…

missions.constraint: Ask about the total and say “I’ll take it.”

Try it on and say how it fits.

teach.goal: Resolver uma compra real com o inglês.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão; alternem vendedor e cliente.
Progressão: com apoio, palavras-chave, sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções prioritárias.
answers: Modelo: “How much are these shoes?” → “Sixty dollars.” → “Do you have these in black?” → “Sorry, only in brown.”
extra: What if the shop is too expensive?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to an online store asking about a size and a color.
pages.model: Hello! **I’m interested in the blue jacket.** **Do you have this in** medium? **How much is** shipping? Thank you!
checklist: I named the item and the color.
I asked about size or price (Do you have…? / How much…?).
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à compra.
solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add a question about returns.

errors.r: How much is it? / I’d like to know the price.

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Language use

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.

Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The structure stays the same; language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: How much is this? Can I try it on?
ladder.goal: Ask the price and try something on.

ladder.say: Do you have this jacket in a smaller size? It’s a little big for me.
ladder.goal: Ask for another size and explain.

ladder.say: I like this one, but it’s over my budget. Is there a cheaper one that looks similar?
I’d like to return this, please. It doesn’t fit properly, and I still have the receipt.
The fit is slightly off around the shoulders, so I’m wondering whether you could suggest an alternative.
ladder.goal: Give precise feedback and ask for advice.

ladder.say: I’m fond of the cut, but the fabric feels a bit stiff; I’d rather keep looking.
ladder.goal: Express taste and a polite refusal.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
